tags.label: C#
tags.summary:
C# is a statically typed, object-oriented language on the .NET runtime. It is the primary scripting language for Unity.

Key features include generics, LINQ, async/await, pattern matching, and nullable reference types.

tags.label: Unity
tags.summary:
Unity is a cross-platform game engine. Scripts inherit from MonoBehaviour and interact with the engine through a defined lifecycle.

Core concepts include GameObjects, Components, Prefabs, Scenes, and the Inspector.

tags.label: Unity Lifecycle
tags.summary:
Unity calls methods on MonoBehaviours in a defined order:
Awake → OnEnable → Start → FixedUpdate → Update → LateUpdate → OnDisable → OnDestroy.

Awake runs even on disabled components. Start is deferred until the component is first enabled. FixedUpdate runs on a fixed time step independent of frame rate.

tags.label: Basics
tags.summary:
Fundamental patterns and practices every developer should know.

Includes Destroy vs DestroyImmediate, GetComponent, DontDestroyOnLoad, null checks on destroyed objects (Unity overrides ==), and why to avoid FindObjectOfType in Update.

tags.label: Object-Oriented Programming
tags.summary:
OOP organises code around objects with data and behaviour. The four pillars are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

C# adds access modifiers (public, private, protected, internal), virtual/override/sealed for polymorphism, and explicit interface implementation for resolving conflicts.

tags.label: Inheritance
tags.summary:
Inheritance lets a class derive from another, reusing and extending its behaviour. C# supports single class inheritance but multiple interface implementation.

Use virtual/override for polymorphic dispatch, the new keyword for method hiding, sealed to prevent further overrides, and base to call parent members.

tags.label: Collections
tags.summary:
C# collections live in System.Collections.Generic.

List<T> is a dynamic array with O(n) Contains. Dictionary<TKey,TValue> is a hash map with O(1) lookup. HashSet<T> is a unique set with O(1) Contains. Queue<T> and Stack<T> handle FIFO and LIFO.

Use TryGetValue to avoid double lookups in dictionaries.

tags.label: ScriptableObjects
tags.summary:
ScriptableObjects are Unity assets that store data independently of scenes. They are shared by reference, not copied like [Serializable] classes.

Changes in Play Mode persist to disk — use Instantiate() for runtime copies. Created via [CreateAssetMenu].

Useful for shared config, event systems, and decoupling.

tags.label: Coroutines
tags.summary:
Coroutines spread work across frames using yield return. They run on the main thread, not multithreaded.

yield return null waits one frame. WaitForSeconds respects timeScale. Disabling the GameObject stops all its coroutines permanently.

Cache WaitForSeconds to avoid per-frame allocations. Use StartCoroutine to nest coroutines.

tags.label: Async / Await
tags.summary:
C# async/await enables asynchronous programming using Tasks. async allows a method to use await, which suspends execution without blocking the thread.

Unlike coroutines, async methods can return values (Task<T>), propagate exceptions via try/catch, and work outside MonoBehaviour.

In Unity, UniTask is preferred for lower allocation overhead.

tags.label: Addressables
tags.summary:
Unity Addressables loads assets by address asynchronously via AsyncOperationHandle. It uses reference counting — every LoadAssetAsync needs a matching Release or the asset leaks.

Assets are organised into Groups (controlling bundling) and can be tagged with Labels for batch loading.

Profiles switch between local/remote load paths. Remote catalogs enable hot-updating assets without app store submissions.

tags.label: Events & Delegates
tags.summary:
Delegates are type-safe function references. Action (void return) and Func (with return value) are built-in generic delegates.

Events wrap delegates with += and -= semantics. Delegates are multicast — subscribing twice calls the handler twice.

Always unsubscribe in OnDisable/OnDestroy to prevent memory leaks and null reference calls on destroyed objects.

tags.label: LINQ
tags.summary:
LINQ provides a fluent API for filtering (Where), transforming (Select), and aggregating (Sum, Count) collections.

It uses deferred execution — queries run only when enumerated (foreach, ToList). Each chained method allocates an iterator on the heap.

Avoid LINQ in Update or other hot paths. Use manual loops for performance-critical code.

tags.label: Memory & Performance
tags.summary:
The .NET GC uses three generations — Gen 0 (short-lived, collected often), Gen 1, and Gen 2 (long-lived, collected rarely).

Heap allocations come from new objects, boxing, closures, and LINQ iterators. Reduce GC pressure with object pooling, structs, caching, Span, and stackalloc.

Implement IDisposable for deterministic cleanup of unmanaged resources. Avoid calling GC.Collect() manually except during loading screens.

tags.label: Physics
tags.summary:
Unity's physics engine runs in FixedUpdate on a fixed time step. Rigidbody controls simulation — apply forces and velocity in FixedUpdate, read input in Update.

isKinematic removes an object from physics simulation while keeping collision/trigger callbacks. Physics.Raycast returns bool with hit data via out RaycastHit.

Use layer masks to filter what rays hit.

tags.label: Design Patterns
tags.summary:
Design patterns are reusable solutions to common problems in game development.

Creational: Factory centralises object creation. Singleton ensures one global instance. Prototype clones existing objects. Object Pool recycles instances to avoid GC.

Behavioural: Command wraps actions as objects for undo/replay. State replaces complex switch chains with state objects. Observer decouples publishers from subscribers. Event Queue spreads event processing over time.

Structural: Component breaks behaviour into reusable pieces (Unity's core architecture). Decorator adds behaviour at runtime without modifying the class. Facade simplifies access to complex subsystems. Flyweight shares data across many instances. Service Locator provides swappable global access to services.

tags.label: SOLID Principles
tags.summary:
Five OOP design principles by Robert C. Martin.

SRP: one class, one reason to change.
OCP: extend behaviour without modifying existing code.
LSP: subtypes must be substitutable for their base type.
ISP: prefer small focused interfaces over large ones.
DIP: depend on abstractions, not concrete implementations.

tags.label: Exception Handling
tags.summary:
C# uses try/catch/finally for structured error handling. finally always runs regardless of exceptions.

Custom exceptions inherit from System.Exception. The when keyword filters catch blocks by condition.

Throwing is expensive (captures full stack trace) — use exceptions for exceptional conditions, not normal control flow. The using statement ensures Dispose is called via try/finally.

tags.label: Profiling & Debugging
tags.summary:
The Unity Profiler shows per-frame CPU, GPU, memory, and rendering breakdowns. The GC Alloc column flags heap allocations in hot paths.

Deep Profile instruments every method (5-10x overhead). Use Profiler.BeginSample/EndSample for targeted measurement.

The Frame Debugger steps through draw calls to diagnose batching and rendering issues. The Memory Profiler package captures detailed snapshots with reference chains.

Always profile on the target device — editor overhead skews results.
